# Astro matrix

<!-- @generated by apps/playground-astro/scripts/matrix.ts from astro-matrix.json: do not edit -->

Every basalt-ui part rendered by `apps/playground-astro` (Astro 7, @astrojs/react, Tailwind 4, the package's built dist) in each render mode and measured in a real browser (shell) on every CI head. This file is the record a run is checked against: each part's verdicts and its byte budgets. The measured run (every size, LCP, CLS, the pixel diffs and side-by-side pictures, the exports no demo renders) is `.astro-matrix/matrix.md`, kept as the `astro-matrix` artifact of the CI run. How to run it and how a budget is raised: `docs/validation.md` § Astro matrix.

## Summary

- **90 parts**, **76** static-clean: the HTML Astro writes with no directive matches the client:only render word for word and to within 4 pixels (a measured flake) at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark.
- **Zero JavaScript without an island:** a page without an island loads no script, checked on every run.
- **The first React island** (React, react-dom and the Astro island runtime, before any basalt code) is budgeted at 72.3 kB of gzip JavaScript.
- **Budgets** are gzip ceilings, set at the size measured then plus 1.0 kB. A run fails past one and never below one; a budget is raised on purpose, with its reason, and an improvement leaves the record as it is.

Columns: `No directive` is the static HTML: `clean`, `differs` from the client:only picture, or `fails` on the server. JavaScript is the most any hydrating mode's page loads; further island is what it loads beyond the baseline island, the cost of adding the part to a page that already has one.

## Several islands on one page

Every part of a family on one page, each its own island, in one mode: the JavaScript budget of each page. Astro sends React once per page; client:visible counts only the islands in the first viewport.

## Charts: is the static picture correct?

Each kind renders in a box of a declared 640 px (the engine's server width, `INITIAL_WIDTH` in `packages/basalt-ui/src/charts/sizing.ts`); at 390 the box is narrower than that. The run's matrix.md gives the share of differing pixels per view and the side-by-side pictures.

## Findings

The cause of each difference, read from the source, and the plan row that carries the fix where the part should need no JavaScript for its picture.

- **lines, bars, cartesian-chart, chart-card, heatmap, interval-track, band-strip**: Correct at the declared width: the server SVG is drawn for the frame the server assumes (`INITIAL_WIDTH`, 640 px, in `packages/basalt-ui/src/charts/sizing.ts`; a `ChartCard` less its two 16 px edges) at the height the box resolves to there (`boxHeightAt` in `box.tsx`, handed to the engine on the server pass only, in `host.tsx`), and the engine measures text from basalt's generated label widths on both sides (`text-measure.ts`), so at 1440 the static picture is the hydrated one to the pixel. The residual is at 390: the box there is 342 px, narrower than the 640 px the server drew for, and HTML rendered before any browser cannot know the viewport, so the browser scales the 640 px picture into the box (the svg's viewBox), with smaller text and a letterbox, until an island redraws it at its measured width; a page with no island keeps the scaled picture. Two more boxes the server cannot know draw the same way: a `fill` box (a ChartCard with `height: 'fill'`, a Heatmap that fills its parent, and each pane of such a card), whose height is its parent's, gets the engine's 320 px; a card stretched by its grid row past its box's floor is drawn at the floor; a coarse pointer's 45svh cap on the box is the viewport's. Sparkline draws its own SVG, scaled per axis, and is static-clean at every width. Hover on top is the same kind as a client:visible island; the engine is most of its 100 to 120 kB further cost.
- **inner-nav, split-page, controls, control-home, app-shell**: App parts: they read field handles or the registered nav from a TanStack Router (no router: "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'stores')", "Invalid value used as weak map key"), on the server and in the browser alike. They are not island parts by contract; an Astro page uses links and the site profile instead.
- **connection-indicator**: Reads `useConnection`, which needs a QueryClient: an app part, not an island part.
- **refresh-button**: The age text is relative to the browser's clock and absent until hydration; a static page cannot know it.
- **dock**: The dock takes focus on mount: the focus ring is the whole difference (0.03%). **Resolved: static-clean now; delete this finding.**

## Not measured

`server:defer` (server islands) is not measured: it needs an adapter and on-demand rendering, and this playground builds static output only.
